stem: In the figure, two lines intersect. What is the value of \(y\)?
solution: The angles labeled \((3x + 10)^{\circ}\) and \((5x - 30)^{\circ}\) are vertical angles, so they are equal: \(3x + 10 = 5x - 30\), which gives \(x = 20\).
The angle labeled \(y^{\circ}\) forms a straight line with the \(70^{\circ}\) angle, so \(y = 180 - 70 = 110\).
verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
x=symbols('x')
xs=solve(Eq(3*x+10,5*x-30),x)[0]
ans=180-(3*xs+10)
assert abs(ang('Q','O','R')-(3*xs+10))<0.1 and abs(ang('P','O','S')-(5*xs-30))<0.1 and abs(ang('R','O','P')-ans)<0.1
assert Rational(spr_answers[0])==ans==110
